text.p: These are the leading stories in Zimbabwe's state-owned Herald newspaper on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Some Z$1.5 billion has been paid out in the last six years through the War Victims' Compensation Fund but most of this money was obtained fraudulently in what has been describedd as potentially the largest looting of public funds in the history of Zimbabwe.

- Senior foreign ministry officials have moved to clear what they say was a misunderstanding with the Japanese government which was angered that its health and welfare minister failed to meet President Robert Mugabe on a visit to Harare last Friday.
- Plans to start work on the Z$7 billion Matebeleland Zambezi Water Project could spark a row between Zimbabwe and Zambia.
- The fourth African/African-American Summit opens amid high expectations from participants who will have a chance to exchange business and procurement information.

- An inquest into the death of prominent local businessman Peter Pamire, who was killed in a car accident earlier this year, opened at the Harare Magistrates Court on Tuesday with his widow giving evidence.
